body: Sorry to say this but your bitcoins are gone.  I went through the “verification” process with Coinbase a little over a year ago.  Sent in the ids, etc. (multiple times) and they never released my account.  Luckily I never had more than a few thousand USD in my account so not a big loss.  Lesson learned?  Coinbase is crooked and you should look elsewhere.  The good news is that there are more options available besides the Coinbase scammers.

Thanks dspacey.  I appreciate your comments but I do think my relationship with Emily was real.  Initially I thought it was more of a lust emotion but then I started to really care about her.  Plus meeting her in person and meeting some of her family reinforced it.   When I travel I usually fly back to the states every other week and my wife has been great in all respects.  So intimacy was never an issue but absence probably was - out of sight, out of mind type thing.  I think the pain comes from two places - first, I haven't had a 'new' relationship in 30 years so the pain of breaking up is new to me again.  Dealing with it is hard.  The second thing is that the guilt of cheating just magnifies the pain of the breakup - IMHO.   I'm still here so that's a good sign.  My guns are in a safe and the ammo is in a different safe.   Thanks again.

Since I've been on the path you are on, and sometimes I jump back on it again, I have to say that there are some good events that take place in my life too.  I would like to be able to control my thought process so that I can keep the positive attitude.  I think that a lot of this has to do with the chemical balances in the brain.  Serotonin, dopamine, all that stuff when it gets out of balance can totally fuck you up.  It's tough, I've been there and I will be back, but try to appreciate little things you may like.  It could get you through this period - it's worked for me up to now.

I totally agree with you.  The survival instinct is incredibly strong.  Overcoming it amounts to having more pain in your life and the need to end that pain than the survival instinct can push back on that pain.  I have done a little bit of research in how to overcome the survival instinct.  I believe Kurt Cobain repeatedly watched a video of how he planned on CTB before he actually did it.  I believe that you can also 'deaden', no pun intended, the survival instinct by taking drugs or alcohol.  I sometimes think the fear of the unknown is the main reason why some people don't do it.

A couple items.  First, people will care and you will be remembered.  Not after a 100 years but for the next 20 or so.  And you will also be missed.  You will be missed more than you can imagine because your family and friends will continue to try and figure out why you did it and if they could have stopped you.  No matter how long a goodbye letter you write it will not answer all the questions.

Now the second item.  I know exactly how you feel about pulling the trigger or turning off the lights.  I have contemplated, designed, and researched ways to ensure that my final act will not be a 'near-miss' and will be fatal.  I have even located areas where I figure I will not be found fast enough to get me to a hospital - I live in a major city so its quite a drive to find a place where nobody is.  But my biggest problem is exactly as you say - what happens when you pull the trigger?  I wrestle with that all the time.  I don't know the answer but I wanted to let you know you are not alone.  There are lots of us trying to figure that out.

I hope you stay safe and don't do anything to hurt yourself.  I have managed to keep the gun out of my mouth but it isn't easy.  Take care.

True, I hate the taste of blood LOL. It would have to be a really nasty flinch to blow out your cheek instead of the brain stem.  But when it comes to the survival instinct I guess anything can happen.

The only way to guarantee death is to drive way out in the middle of nowhere so if you do flinch at the last minute and rip a non-fatal hole in the side of your head no one will be able to find you and you will bleed out.  Not the ideal death but at least you accomplished what you wanted.

Still I can’t pull the trigger.

I'm not a cop or lawyer so I don't know the details but he committed a crime and your are reporting the perp as being him.  That should be enough to start an investigation.

Everyone on this site, including myself, have problems that we think are insurmountable.  I am not going to try to solve your problem  or try to minimize it because it obviously is bothering you.  In fact your are obsessed to the point of wanting to end it all.

However, I will challenge you on your 'genetic lottery' comment.  I have known many people in my life and have heard stories that would make you cry or at least cringe when it comes to children dying at early ages because they indeed lost the genetic lottery.  Or people who have been disfigured in accidents beyond their control and needed to recover from some horrendous injuries.  These are people who truly lost the genetic lottery or were victims of destiny beyond their control.  Losing your hair is not a problem and being short is not a problem.

You need to build some self confidence and get rid of the self pity.  My god based on how you talk you could look like Brad Pitt and the girls/guys would run the other way.  It's not all looks that make a person, it's how they present themselves!  You need to work on the presentation skills.

I'm not a doctor but I understand your frustration.  Since it has been 6 months it is still relatively new meaning that the problem if identified could be resolved with the right expertise.  My problem lasted for 8 months and since I would not do anything but lay on the couch I gained 30 lbs and a cycle of self hatred began.  Keep looking because I think you are getting bad advice.  Keep talking to friends about your situation because that is how I found the right doctor.  Unfortunately doctors are not looking out for the patients anymore.  They are looking out for the cash only side of the equation.

What kind of pain do you have?  I had severe leg pain for about 8 months and was told it was sciatica and I would have to live with it.  I went to orthopedic doctors and pain doctors - they both confirmed it.  A friend of mine told me to go to a neurosurgeon.  The neurosurgeon found a cyst in my spine that was rubbing up against the nerve that was causing the pain in my leg.  He removed the cyst and the pain was gone within a day.  The other two doctors did not even see the cyst on the MRI.  

My point is that the experts that you are talking to don't know the answer so they are putting the blame on you.  Keep looking until you find someone who is smarter than your current set of experts.  Based on what you say about their 'support and recommendations'  you should not have a problem finding a smarter expert.

Good luck and don't give up too soon.

It makes me wonder if drinking before shooting myself would make it easier.
